reasons: Factual predicate checks out: the term clause (p0011) is evergreen with termination under § 6, § 6(a) gives a 15-day at-will exit, and no auto-renewal, renewal term or non-renewal notice window appears in the document — so the renewal-mechanics limbs are genuinely satisfied and the rendered check confirms an effective window of 30 days (≤ 60).

The residual deviation is correctly identified and in-scope for this parametric rule, which expressly covers 'price uplift language' and requires ongoing pricing predictability: § 3(b) (p0014) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped, unlimited-frequency right to raise rates on 30 days' notice, which is the only pricing-uplift lever in an evergreen deal.

Redline is directionally correct for the customer and additive rather than destructive: it preserves the existing 30-day notice bargain and appends only the playbook cap (once per 12 months; lesser of CPI and 3%) plus a fix of rates in already-executed Statements of Work. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic reflects appended proviso length, not an unnecessary rewrite of the clause.

The SOW rate-fix is well-targeted to the actual exposure, since the § 6(a) convenience exit is only available when no Statement of Work is outstanding, leaving Company unable to escape a mid-SOW increase.

Comment is accurate and correctly scoped: it states there is no auto-renewal, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position on predictable pricing, and offers the 5% fallback in line with the rule's fallback tier. Tone and prefix conform.
